leads.date: 1945 (patent filed); first ovens sold 1947; countertop models 1967
leads.why: Microwave heating made reheating and ready meals a matter of minutes in hundreds of millions of kitchens.

leads.title: Seed-crop farming in eastern North America
leads.where: Mississippi, Ohio and Tennessee river valleys, United States
leads.why: Woodland societies domesticated sunflower, marshelder, goosefoot and a native squash and farmed them for two thousand years before maize arrived; sunflower became a world oil crop.
leads.verify: The earliest dated domesticated specimens of each crop and their sites (Phillips Spring, Hayes, Napoleon Hollow, Riverton); confirmation that this complex arose before any Mesoamerican crop reached the region; when and why most of these crops were abandoned.

leads.title: Potato farming in northern Europe
leads.where: Ireland, the Low Countries and Prussia
leads.date: arrived c. 1570; a field staple c. 1700–1800
leads.why: Europeans selected the Andean potato to form tubers under long summer days; it fed the population growth behind industrialisation, and its failure in the 1840s founded plant pathology.
leads.verify: The first records of potatoes in Europe (Canary Islands and Seville, 1560s–1570s); how and when long-day adapted varieties arose; estimates of the potato's effect on European population.

leads.title: Transgenic crop plants in Belgium and the United States
leads.where: Ghent, Belgium; St. Louis, Missouri, United States
leads.why: Gene transfer into plants produced the insect-resistant and herbicide-tolerant crops now grown on over a tenth of the world's cropland and opened plant biotechnology.
leads.verify: The three groups that reported transgenic plant cells or plants in 1983 (Ghent, Washington University, Monsanto) and their publication dates; the first field trials and commercial releases. The existing recombinant plasmid cloning record is the prerequisite, not this.

leads.why: Kava was domesticated in Vanuatu and carried by canoe to Fiji, Polynesia and parts of Micronesia, where its shared drinking structures ceremony and politics.
leads.verify: The botanical and genetic case for domestication from Piper wichmannii in northern Vanuatu; any archaeological date at all, since the timing rests on inference; the routes of its spread.

leads.title: Pure yeast culture brewing in Copenhagen
leads.why: Brewing from a single isolated yeast cell ended spoiled batches, became standard in brewing worldwide and set the method for industrial microbiology.
leads.verify: Hansen's isolation of single yeast strains and the first production brew with pure yeast at Carlsberg in 1883; how quickly other breweries adopted it; its relation to Pasteur's and Koch's methods.

concepts.name: Crop introduction
concepts.summary: Establishing a staple crop brought from a distant region and adapting it and the local farming system to each other.

concepts.name: Kava
concepts.summary: Preparing a calming drink from the pounded or chewed root of the kava plant and sharing it in a set social form.

concepts.name: Microwave oven
concepts.summary: An oven that heats food from within by exposing it to microwave radiation.

concepts.name: Plant domestication
concepts.summary: Turning wild plants into crops through human selection and cultivation, so that they depend on people and yield more.

concepts.name: Pure-culture fermentation
concepts.summary: Fermenting with a single selected strain of microbe grown from one cell, so that the product is the same every time.

concepts.name: Transgenic crops
concepts.summary: Crop plants given genes from other organisms by laboratory gene transfer rather than by crossing.
